title: Replacing Just 10 Percent of Ultra‑processed Foods with Whole Foods Linked to Drop in Bowel Cancer Rate - Nautilus
gist: An analysis of data from more than 460,000 US adults links replacing 10% of ultra-processed food with minimally processed food to 2% lower bowel cancer incidence, though total ultra-processed intake itself showed no association.

insights.claim: Replacing 10% of ultra-processed food intake with minimally processed foods was linked to 2% lower bowel cancer incidence in data from more than 460,000 US adults.
insights.speaker: Erikka Loftfield
insights.so_what: Small effect size; supports modest whole-food substitution messaging.

insights.claim: Total ultra-processed food intake showed no association with bowel cancer incidence.
insights.speaker: Erikka Loftfield
insights.so_what: Complicates blanket ultra-processed food risk narratives.
insights.locator: However, we also found no association

insights.claim: Wholegrains, fibre, dairy and calcium from ultra-processed sources were associated with lower bowel cancer incidence, while ultra-processed meats were associated with higher incidence.
insights.speaker: Erikka Loftfield
insights.so_what: Risk appears driven by food type, such as processed meats, rather than processing level alone.
